name: Pendulum swing
equipment: a table or chair back to lean on
movement: bent forward with the arm hanging, swung gently in small circles

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you, the arm you are swinging nearest the camera.

words.hint: Bent forward with one hand on a table, the other arm hanging loose and swinging in small circles.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Lean forward with one hand on a table, side on to it, and let the other arm hang.
words.position: Stand side on to the phone, bend forward from the hips with the good hand on a table or chair back, and let the stiff arm hang straight down, relaxed.
words.top: The trunk leaning forward — anywhere from halfway to nearly flat — the arm hanging straight and loose, swinging small circles about a foot across, moved by the body, not the shoulder.
howto: Stand with one foot forward and the knees soft. Lean forward from the hips with your good hand on a table, so the stiff arm hangs clear of your body.
Let the arm hang heavy. Rock your body gently so the arm swings in small circles, about a foot across — the shoulder muscles do nothing.
Keep it going for the count. Ten circles each way, then the other direction.
As it eases over the weeks, widen the circles a little or hold a light weight. Never force it.
words.cannot: Whether the shoulder muscles are truly relaxed, and the side-to-side part of the swing, which is toward the camera: it sees the lean, the arm’s forward-and-back swing and the elbow. The arm should feel heavy, like a rope.
words.about: Pendulum swing — standing side on, bent forward with the good hand on a table: the lean, as the hip-to-shoulder line off vertical, 30–95° (from halfway to nearly flat, enough for the arm to hang clear); the arm, as how far the shoulder-to-wrist line is lifted from hanging straight down, at most 23° — circles a foot across stay well inside it, more is the shoulder lifting the arm rather than the body swinging it; and the elbow at least 150°, the arm hanging straight. The clock runs while all three are right. Thirty seconds a set, three sets.
words.lost: Stand side on to the camera, bent forward, the whole body in
words.hold: That is it — let it swing
words.safety: Pain-free only: the pendulum is the gentlest frozen-shoulder exercise and should stay that way. Stop if it sharpens.
words.harder: Wider circles; a light weight (one to two kilos) in the hand; a longer time.
words.mistakes: Using the shoulder muscles to swing the arm; standing too upright so the arm rubs the body; bending the elbow; holding the breath.

measurements.label: trunk lean
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off vertical, + forward: 0 upright, 90 flat. Bent 40–80 the arm hangs clear of the body.

settings.label: Trunk lean, at least (degrees from upright)

measurements.label: arm off hanging
measurements.why: How far the shoulder-to-wrist line is lifted from straight down: 0 hanging plumb. A pendulum swing a foot across stays under 20; past 35 the arm is being lifted by the shoulder.

settings.label: Arm off hanging straight down, at most (degrees)

measurements.label: elbow straight
measurements.why: The arm hanging straight: 180 is straight; under 150 the elbow is bent and the arm is being held.

settings.label: Elbow angle, at least (180 is straight)

faults.label: Lean further
faults.text: Lean forward a little more, hand on the table — the arm has to hang clear
faults.deep: Bend further forward from the hips — the arm has to hang clear of your body

faults.label: Too far down
faults.text: Come up a little — anywhere from halfway to nearly flat is fine

faults.label: Arm lifting
faults.text: Let the arm hang — swing it with your body, not your shoulder
faults.deep: The arm is being lifted — drop it, let it hang heavy, and rock your body instead
